ai.description: This small skink reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It is brown with a pale lateral stripe and possesses a notably large, exposed tympanum. It lacks the distinct dark mid-lateral band of similar species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Lipinia macrotympanum* is uniquely distinguished by its exceptionally large, conspicuous external ear opening, which is significantly more prominent than in other Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: *Lipinia macrotympanum* inhabits the dense, humid evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found at low to moderate elevations within the leaf litter or on trees.
ai.behavior: The Big-eared Lipinia is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and decaying logs within its tropical forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lipinia macrotympanum* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lipinia macrotympanum* is endemic to the evergreen forests of Northeast India, specifically found in the states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam at low elevations.
